title.narrative: EU4Environment - Mainstreaming and Circular Economy - Results 1 and 2

description.narrative: The EU4Environment Action aims to bring a higher level of environmental well-being for citizens in the Eastern Neighbourhood while also helping the six partner countries to grasp opportunities of greener economic growth and preserve their natural capital. UNIDO (with UNECE and UNE as partners) will take responsibility for Results 1 and 2 that aim at promoting higher resource efficiency of economies in the Eastern partner countries and integrate environmental goals into economic development.

comment.narrative: Two baseline countries where capacities to apply SEA and EIA are considered adequate are Georgia and Ukraine see also Comments section. Together with the above the two other countries Azerbaijan and the Republic of Moldova compose the final target of 4 countries under this Outcome. These are the two countries where the capacities to apply particularly SEA were considered not yet sufficient at the start of the EU4Environment. As per an informal assessment by the project team at UNECE also taking into consideration the countries national reporting for 2019 2021 as of early 2023 both Azerbaijan and the Republicof Moldova have not yet built adequate capacities to apply SEA while the application of EIA is operational. ClarificationsTwo baseline countries where capacities to apply SEA and EIA are considered adequate are Georgia and Ukraine. Both countries have appropriate legislation in place for several years which is fully aligned with the respective EU Directives the Espoo Convention and its Protocol on SEA. Sectoral Ministries other relevant authorities and the Ministries of Environment have been applying the respective legislation reasonably effectively to conduct SEAs of strategic documents on a routine basis.Azerbaijan and the Republic of Moldova are the two countries where the capacities to apply SEA were considered not yet sufficient at the start of the EU4Environment. Together with the two baseline countries they compose the final target of four 4 countries under this Outcome. While the implementation of EIA is of lesser concern in Azerbaijan and the Republic of Moldova the SEA practice is still emerging and rather weak. The final target i.e. 4 countries is not yet assured to be reached as regards adequate capacities for SEA by the project end due to several factors 1 Azerbaijan and Moldova adopted amended primary legislation RM and new secondary implementing legislation AZ only in 2022 which requires some time to be familiarized with and be effectively applied by sectoral and other relevant authorities. Further to that in the case of RM the adopted amended laws will enter into force only in late 2023. 2 Capacity gaps still remain large. Departmentsunits within the Ministries and Environment Agency RM lack humanexpert resources experience high staff turnover and therefore cannot fully fulfil the demanding roles to coordinate the SEA procedures. 3 Sectoralline Ministries seem to continue to lack sufficient awareness on SEA most uptodate national legislative requirements and the roles they are expected to perform in SEA procedures.4 While there is a larger pool of EIA practitionersexperts this is not the case for those knowledgeable about SEA as the SEA practice is still emerging and not yet consolidated rather few SEAs are conducted in these two countries and the quality aspects of those SEA vary.

comment.narrative: Two baseline countries where capacities to apply SEA and EIA are considered adequate are Georgia and Ukraine see also Comments section. Together with the above the two other countries Azerbaijan and the Republic of Moldova compose the final target of 4 countries under this Outcome. These are the two countries where the capacities to apply particularly SEA were considered not yet sufficient at the start of the EU4Environment. As per an informal assessment by the project team at UNECE also taking into consideration the countries national reporting for 2019 2021 as of early 2023 both Azerbaijan and the Republicof Moldova have not yet built adequate capacities to apply SEA while the application of EIA is operational. ClarificationsTwo baseline countries where capacities to apply SEA and EIA are considered adequate are Georgia and Ukraine. Both countries have appropriate legislation in place for several years which is fully aligned with the respective EU Directives the Espoo Convention and its Protocol on SEA. Sectoral Ministries other relevant authorities and the Ministries of Environment have been applying the respective legislation reasonably effectively to conduct SEAs of strategic documents on a routine basis.Azerbaijan and the Republic of Moldova are the two countries where the capacities to apply SEA were considered not yet sufficient at the start of the EU4Environment. Together with the two baseline countries they compose the final target of four 4 countries under this Outcome. While the implementation of EIA is of lesser concern in Azerbaijan and the Republic of Moldova the SEA practice is still emerging and rather weak. The final target i.e. 4 countries is not yet assured to be reached as regards adequate capacities for SEA by the project end due to several factors 1 Azerbaijan and Moldova adopted amended primary legislation RM and new secondary implementing legislation AZ only in 2022 which requires some time to be familiarized with and be effectively applied by sectoral and other relevant authorities. Further to that in the case of RM the adopted amended laws will enter into force only in late 2023. 2 Capacity gaps still remain large. Departmentsunits within the Ministries and Environment Agency RM lack humanexpert resources experience high staff turnover and therefore cannot fully fulfil the demanding roles to coordinate the SEA procedures. 3 Sectoralline Ministries seem to continue to lack sufficient awareness on SEA most uptodate national legislative requirements and the roles they are expected to perform in SEA procedures.4 While there is a larger pool of EIA practitionersexperts this is not the case for those knowledgeable about SEA as the SEA practice is still emerging and not yet consolidated rather few SEAs are conducted in these two countries and the quality aspects of those SEA vary.

comment.narrative: Out of the three SEA pilot projects 1 Armenia 1 Azerbaijan and 1 Georgia that were under way in 2022 two countries Armenia Dec 2022 Jan 2023 and Georgia in Sept 2022 requested to discontinue the further implementation of the pilot projects due to external circumstances that precluded implementationsuccessful completion. Ukraine withdrew its initially proposed focus of the pilot project hydrogen strategy in August 2022 replaced it with a provisional new proposal in Dec 2022 and finally requested to replace the pilot project with another activity i.e. SEA trainings due to war circumstances in February 2023 official correspondence on this from Ukraines Ministry of Environment provided on 14 February 2023 and the request granted based on consultations with the EU. The Republic of Moldova which proposed an industries development programme for the SEA pilot project in May 2022 did not provide any draftconcept in 2022 to enable further implementation of the pilot as the Ministry of Economy finalized the draft concept and cleared it for release only on 7 February 2023. This made it possible to implement only limited further steps beyond hiring SEA experts etc. of the pilot in 2022 in absence of any strategic document draftconcept subject to SEA. The final concept of the programme a very short and rather general document by itself is too general to enable the SEA scoping but it enables the development of a first draft programme expected to be available by the end of June 2023. Consequently the SEA scoping is to be based on the first draft programme. The pilot is expected to be completed in fall 2023. In Azerbaijan the pilot project SEA for a draft master plan of the city of Ganja is expected to be finalized over summer 2023 as the State Committee on Urban Planning and Architecture continued to develop the draft master plan with significant additions to the draft in JanApril 2023.

description.narrative: 1.3.5 Number of additional pilot projects implemented

comment.narrative: Out of the three SEA pilot projects 1 Armenia 1 Azerbaijan and 1 Georgia that were under way in 2022 two countries Armenia Dec 2022 Jan 2023 and Georgia in Sept 2022 requested to discontinue the further implementation of the pilot projects due to external circumstances that precluded implementationsuccessful completion. Ukraine withdrew its initially proposed focus of the pilot project hydrogen strategy in August 2022 replaced it with a provisional new proposal in Dec 2022 and finally requested to replace the pilot project with another activity i.e. SEA trainings due to war circumstances in February 2023 official correspondence on this from Ukraines Ministry of Environment provided on 14 February 2023 and the request granted based on consultations with the EU. The Republic of Moldova which proposed an industries development programme for the SEA pilot project in May 2022 did not provide any draftconcept in 2022 to enable further implementation of the pilot as the Ministry of Economy finalized the draft concept and cleared it for release only on 7 February 2023. This made it possible to implement only limited further steps beyond hiring SEA experts etc. of the pilot in 2022 in absence of any strategic document draftconcept subject to SEA. The final concept of the programme a very short and rather general document by itself is too general to enable the SEA scoping but it enables the development of a first draft programme expected to be available by the end of June 2023. Consequently the SEA scoping is to be based on the first draft programme. The pilot is expected to be completed in fall 2023. In Azerbaijan the pilot project SEA for a draft master plan of the city of Ganja is expected to be finalized over summer 2023 as the State Committee on Urban Planning and Architecture continued to develop the draft master plan with significant additions to the draft in JanApril 2023.
